A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SVIP and provide readable text, equations, algorithms, tables, figures, and references. All pages were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original SVIP evaluations on CUB, AwA2, and SUN, including component ablations, hyperparameter sweeps, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and analyses, with revised quantitative results in Tables 1 and 2.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same attention aggregation, patch classifier, semantic contextualization, attribute localization, two-pass training objective, and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CUB, AwA2, and SUN under conventional and generalized zero-shot learning. No additional dataset, domain, or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 1 substantially revises its ResNet101 comparison block: TF, APN, GEM, and ICCE are removed, while CANZSL and HAS are added. The six ViT comparators and Table 2's ablation comparator set remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain the same class splits, T1/U/S/H metrics, ImageNet-1k-pretrained ViT-base, 224-by-224 inputs, and aggregation into 49 patches. No changed evaluation protocol or experimental setting is reported.

E4.justification: The five component ablations, four hyperparameter sweeps, attention analyses, and qualitative visualizations test the same questions in both versions. Revised ablation scores are numerical-result changes; no analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both present point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 revise SVIP's H from 76.1/75.5/51.2 to 75.0/74.9/50.7 on CUB/AwA2/SUN, retaining its leading H rankings. Table 2 also revises SUN without W2P, including H from 50.8 to 50.1; other ablation rows remain fixed, so full SVIP no longer leads every metric. Table 1 also adds and removes baseline result rows.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and Equations 1–14 are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical guarantees, proofs, or revised mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: addressing semantic misalignment at the input stage through patch selection and contextualization, with claimed state-of-the-art benchmark performance.

C2.justification: v2 removes the ablation conclusion that the full model achieves the best results everywhere and thereby demonstrates every module's contribution to alignment and performance. The remaining mechanism explanations and qualitative interpretations are retained; no substantive limitations discussion is added.

D1.justification: v2 newly provides a GitHub code-availability link in the abstract. Algorithm 1 and Section 4.1 otherwise provide the same implementation information.

R1.justification: The bibliography adds 21 works and removes the two references underlying TF and ICCE. Section 2 introduces broad citation coverage of hashing, point-cloud completion, image editing, adaptation, disease recognition, and video retrieval, plus two additional ZSL works. This substantially expands the cited literature, although SVIP's novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammatical corrections, shortens the ablation and sensitivity discussion, updates affiliations and the equal-contribution footnote, and adds an acknowledgment. Section order and most explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 changes row composition, adds SVIP's venue, and updates ranking highlights. The Figure 6 caption receives a wording correction, and author information and end matter reflow. All seven figure graphics and the overall two-column design are retained.

improvement.justification: The code-access statement and narrower ablation conclusion help, but v2 introduces reporting inconsistencies: Section 4.2 still names APN, GEM, and ICCE as Table 1 comparators after removing them. Its P2A discussion also does not acknowledge SUN's reversed unseen-accuracy ranking, 53.8 without P2A versus 53.7 for full SVIP. These benefits and harms, together with unexplained score revisions, leave the net quality change uncertain.
